definition: An instance profile delivers temporary, auto-rotated role credentials to an EC2 instance. Remember: never store access keys on instances; attach a role instead.
Credentials report lists every user and their password, key and MFA status account-wide. Access Advisor shows which services one identity actually used, to trim permissions.
Access keys let the CLI and SDKs call AWS as an IAM user. Treat them like passwords. Remember: prefer roles and CloudShell over long-term keys.
A managed policy that sets the maximum permissions a user or role can get. It grants nothing by itself. Remember: stops developers creating over-privileged roles.
Organizations guardrail that limits what member accounts can do, even their root users. It grants nothing and never affects the management account.
An explicit deny anywhere wins. Otherwise the action must pass organization policies, permissions boundaries and session policies, and be allowed by an identity or resource-based policy.
Condition key that allows access only to principals from accounts in your organization. Remember: one bucket policy line covers all current and future accounts.
Assuming a role replaces your original permissions for that session. A resource-based policy lets you keep them. Remember: needed to read in one account and write in another.
Organizations policies that standardize tag keys, capitalization and allowed values across accounts and report noncompliant resources. Remember: fixes messy cost allocation tags.
Formerly AWS SSO. One sign-in for all accounts in an organization and business apps, using permission sets. Identity source: built-in, Active Directory, or an external provider like Entra ID.
Real Microsoft Active Directory run by AWS across two Availability Zones. Supports trusts with on-premises AD. Users stored in it can still sign in if the on-premises link fails.
AD Connector is a proxy to on-premises AD and stores nothing in AWS. Simple AD is a cheap standalone directory that cannot trust on-premises AD.
Sets up a governed multi-account landing zone on Organizations. Preventive controls use service control policies, detective controls use AWS Config, with a compliance dashboard.
AWS owned keys are invisible and free. AWS managed keys rotate yearly automatically. Customer managed keys give you key policies, optional rotation and cross-account sharing.
KMS Encrypt handles only about 4 kilobytes. For bigger data, GenerateDataKey returns a data key that encrypts locally. Remember: large files mean envelope encryption.
Related keys in several Regions sharing one key ID and key material, so data encrypted in one Region decrypts in another. Each replica is managed independently, not global.
Share the AMI or snapshot and grant the other account use of the customer managed key in its key policy. AWS managed keys cannot be shared across accounts.
A bucket-level key that generates data keys locally for SSE-KMS. Remember: cuts KMS request costs and throttling for high-volume S3 buckets.
Standard parameters are free, up to 4 kilobytes. Advanced cost extra, allow 8 kilobytes and parameter policies like expiration. SecureString encrypts with KMS. No built-in rotation.
Stores secrets with a per-secret monthly charge and rotates them automatically, natively for RDS, Aurora, Redshift and DocumentDB. Remember: rotation requirement means Secrets Manager.
Free public TLS certificates that auto-renew on load balancers, CloudFront and API Gateway. Imported certificates do not auto-renew. Remember: CloudFront certificates must be in us-east-1.
Single-tenant hardware security modules in your VPC. You alone manage the keys; AWS cannot see them. Remember: exclusive control or dedicated HSM means CloudHSM.
Layer 7 firewall with web ACLs on CloudFront, Application Load Balancer, API Gateway, AppSync and Cognito. Blocks SQL injection, cross-site scripting, geographies and floods with rate-based rules.
Standard is free, automatic layer 3 and 4 protection. Advanced is paid, adds the Shield Response Team, application layer mitigation and DDoS cost protection.
Centrally applies WAF rules, Shield Advanced, security groups and Network Firewall policies across all accounts in an organization, including new ones automatically.
GuardDuty detects threats from logs like crypto mining. Inspector scans EC2, container images and Lambda for vulnerabilities. Macie finds personal data in S3.
